response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software developer (15+ years) with strong skills in TypeScript, Node.js, DLang, and testing practices, but the resume shows essentially no overlap with the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role: no SoC or IP modeling, no AI accelerator or GPU architecture work, no deep-learning training/inference optimization, and no hardware-software co-design at the silicon level. The closest adjacencies are low-latency microservices at Sociomantic, C/C++ work on LabWindows/CVI at National Instruments, and a wave-field-synthesis audio thesis — none of which approach principal-level hardware architecture depth. Education is a BS in Computer Science, which meets the 8+ years experience path formally, but the domain expertise gap is too large to close through interview.
strengths: 15+ years of broad software engineering experience across domains
Some systems/low-latency and C/C++ embedded exposure (Sociomantic, National Instruments)
Strong open-source, community, and technical communication track record
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling or hardware architecture experience
No AI accelerator, GPU, or deep-learning workload optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not principal-level hardware IC

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI/deep-learning accelerator or GPU workload expertise
Extensive general software engineering tenure and systems-level exposure
